status: Complete: existing-cache analysis only; no new engine evaluation, match games, learner feedback, or experiment mutations.
validation: All 453 cached games matched frozen-ledger UCI move sequences, model/opponent actors, learner color, normal starting position, run alias, and continuity of cached evaluation perspective.
primary_comparison: First versus second half of each cached prefix. Exclude full-strength games for bounded_halves. Standardize exact opponent/config/color using pooled game-count weights; equal weight per game within strata. Bootstrap games, with six-game-block sensitivity for Astra/Opus.

findings.hypothesis: Astra's falling benchmark results reflect deterioration in actual move quality.
findings.assessment: Supported observationally, especially after the first 12 own moves; not evidence for a particular causal mechanism.
findings.evidence: Matched balanced-position moves losing >=200cp: 4.085% to 6.864%; delta +2.779 percentage points, six-game-block 95% interval +1.295 to +4.306. First/last-third sensitivity: 3.572% to 7.027%, interval for delta +1.864 to +5.165. Opening proxy loss and balanced first12 error changes remain uncertain.

findings.hypothesis: Opus's increasing benchmark results demonstrate broad improvement in chess decision quality.
findings.assessment: Only weakly corroborated by the available quality controls.
findings.evidence: Matched balanced-position >=200cp errors: 5.207% to 4.204%; delta -1.003 percentage points, six-game-block interval -2.718 to +0.670. First12 proxy loss 2.431 to 2.476, interval for delta -0.637 to +0.730. Legacy all-move clipped ACPL improves 57.257 to 47.863, but interval for delta -21.889 to +2.906 and saturation/position-mix confounding remain. First/last-third all-move metrics improve more clearly; balanced controls still remain uncertain.

findings.hypothesis: All-move average centipawn loss provides a clean learning measure.
findings.evidence: The legacy score clips both evaluations to +/-1000cp, making already decided positions appear inexpensive. Opus's first/last-third share of moves already at |eval|>=1000cp rises 12.35% to 19.12%; balanced-position share falls 50.83% to 41.47%. Improved whole-game ACPL can therefore combine better outcomes with more saturated winning positions; it is not a clean estimate of improved decision quality.

findings.hypothesis: A higher nominal Stockfish Elo necessarily transfers to stronger play against other opponents.
findings.assessment: The separate head-to-head warns against this interpretation; it does not establish reward hacking.
findings.evidence: Astra won the completed public 30-game match 24.5-5.5 (22 wins, 5 draws, 3 losses), scoring 13/15 with White and 11.5/15 with Black. All 3115 public moves replayed legally. Both used declared Max effort, native post-200 conversations, copied notes, and permitted between-game adaptation; the match was untimed and independent of the Stockfish Elo chart.

limits: No cache-based claim about the late completed Sol, Sol-long, Fable, or Sol-long-max runs is justified.
Tiny-prefix strata yield misleadingly narrow or degenerate resampling intervals; diagnostics explicitly flag them.
Balanced-position selection and later-phase survival depend on prior play. First12 controls include shorter games and explicit exposure counts, but do not randomize positions.
The cached 200k-node review lacks per-evaluation depth, engine fingerprint, node-count, and date fields; the source script does not explicitly clear engine transposition tables.
Head-to-head is not a frozen-policy transfer evaluation, has no before-200 baseline, and may reflect styles, retained context, compute differences, and ongoing adaptation.
These findings do not identify cheating, prohibited tool use, benchmark exploitation, or reward hacking. Legitimate opponent-specific adaptation remains compatible with them.
